title: He was already chosen…
paragraphs: Because there’s something terrifying about being seen by God…
God called Saul king—before Saul believed he could be one. In 1 Samuel 10:22, when the moment came, they had to ask the Lord where he was… and the answer cut deep:
“He has hidden himself among the baggage.”
And suddenly… it’s not just Saul’s story anymore.
Because some of us aren’t running from sin—

We’re hiding behind past failures, silent shame, and that quiet voice that whispers,
“You’re not ready.”
“You’re not worthy.”
“You’ll mess this up.”
We shrink back in moments God said “step forward.”
…but deep down, it’s fear wearing a spiritual mask.
What has God already spoken over your life that you keep postponing?
What step of obedience are you dressing up as “discernment” when it’s actually disobedience?
And here’s the part we don’t say out loud—

Some of us are more comfortable hiding in insecurity
than standing in responsibility.

Because if you never step out…
you never have to risk failing.
Because 1 Samuel 9:21 shows Saul already wrestling with identity—he literally says, “Am I not from the smallest tribe… the least of all the families?” Translation:
And maybe that’s your internal dialogue too.

“I’m not that spiritual.”
“I still struggle.”
“I’ve messed up too much.”
God didn’t call Saul because he was confident.
God called Saul because God had already decided.
Calling is not the reward for your confidence.
It’s the invitation to trust His.
But here’s where it gets heavy.
Saul never fully dealt with that insecurity.
Because insecurity, when left unchecked, turns into people-pleasing… and people-pleasing always leads to disobedience.
In 1 Samuel 15:24, Saul finally admits, “I feared the people and obeyed their voice.”
We don’t realize our spiritual stagnation isn’t because we lack calling—
it’s because we crave approval more than obedience.
Because this isn’t just about Saul.
standing in between hiding and becoming.
You can be anointed… and still be avoiding.
You can be called… and still be controlled by fear.
You can be positioned… and still be paralyzed by shame.
Saying “God is good” means nothing if you keep saying “no” to what He asked you to do.
But here’s where grace breaks in.
Where Saul hid, Jesus stepped forward.
Where Saul feared people, Jesus feared the Father.
Where Saul protected his image, Jesus surrendered His life.
Philippians 2:8 tells us Jesus “humbled Himself by becoming obedient to the point of death—even death on a cross.”
We are all guilty of hiding.
Even the ones sitting quietly in church, battling silent compromise.
But God didn’t leave us there.
Romans 5:8 declares that while we were still sinners—still hiding—Christ died for us.
While we were still in the baggage.
Jesus didn’t wait for you to come out of hiding.
He stepped into your hiding place.
And then walked out of the grave so you could walk out of hiding.
You are not the voice in your head telling you you’re unqualified.
You are who God says you are.
But it does not excuse staying there.

Because the same God who saved you
is calling you forward.
Out of that quiet compromise nobody sees.
And what you’re afraid of stepping into…
might be the very place God’s power shows up.
If this hit something deep in you…
Whisper this prayer if you mean it:
“Jesus, I’m done hiding. I surrender. Lead me.”
We’re exposing the silent ways insecurity disguises itself as “humility.” Don’t miss it.
